title: Velocity Guard Mesh: Latency-aware optimizer and SLO routing for safe batching/caching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our automated batching/caching recommender can produce config changes that reduce token cost but sometimes regress tail latency and throughput under specific traffic shapes (spiky small-requests, long-context sessions, or KV cache fragmentation). We need a guard system that can (1) propose optimizer changes, (2) stage them with SLO-aware routing, (3) detect anomalies quickly, and (4) perform deterministic, safe rollback if SLOs are breached.

Goal: Build the Velocity Guard Mesh (VGM) — a lightweight orchestration layer that sits between the optimizer and the runtime apply path. VGM must provide: staged apply semantics, percentile-based SLO checks, traffic-slice routing (by route/model/customer cohort), per-change circuit limiters, anomaly detectors (statistical + ML baseline), and an automated rollback/fallback policy with audit logs. The system should allow human-in-the-loop for high-risk changes and fully-automated for low-risk configs.

Scope: Implement core orchestration, integrate with Console metrics and tracing, add guard rules for 95th/99th latency and per-GPU throughput, expose orchestration events to audit logs, and run canary experiments on Dedicated pools. This ticket covers the engineering design, prototype implementation for the runtime control plane, and a beta rollout to two internal services (chat-api, embedder-service).
acceptance_criteria: VGM can accept optimizer suggestions and stage them as 'proposal' with metadata and a unique change-id
Traffic can be split per-change-id and routed using routing policies (percentage, cohort, or route-level selectors)
SLO checks evaluate 95th and 99th latency and aggregate throughput over 1m and 5m windows; thresholds configured per-route
Automatic rollback triggers when: latency > threshold for 3 consecutive 1m windows OR throughput drops > 20% sustained for 5m
Anomaly detection flags sudden distribution shifts (KL divergence > configured threshold) and surfaces a signal in Console
All change lifecycle events (propose, apply, canary, escalate, rollback) are emitted to audit logs and linked in the ticket
Beta rollout executed against chat-api and embedder-service with zero impact to external customers (internal traffic only)
Runbook documented and SRE run through a simulated rollback drill
implementation_notes: We will implement the control-plane orchestration as a small state machine service (stateless API + redis for ephemeral change state).
Routing hook: runtime will accept a 'change-id' header and consult VGM for routing decision; fallback to default router if VGM unreachable.
Metrics aggregation will reuse Console's per-route telemetry; will add lightweight derived metrics for canary windows (1m/5m aggregates).
Anomaly detection: initial phase uses statistical tests (moving-window percentiles + KL divergence) and a simple gradient detector; future phase will add a trained detector in Research.
Rollbacks are executed as inverse operations with a tombstone event; each rollback requires a reason and automatically opens a postmortem draft link template.
risk_and_tradeoffs: Introducing an orchestration layer adds an additional dependency for routing; mitigate by making VGM optional and implementing client-side timeouts and fallbacks.
Aggressive automation can cause oscillation (flip-flopping); mitigate via cooldown windows, minimum apply durations, and circuit breakers per route.
Statelessness keeps service easy to scale but increases reliance on Redis for ephemeral state; we'll shard and use TTLs to limit stale proposals.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + integration tests with mock metrics backfill
Phase 1 (internal canary): enable VGM for 3 internal routes (chat-api dev, embedder-service dev, infra-test) at 5% traffic
Phase 2 (beta): expand to staging services 10-20% with automatic rollback enabled
Phase 3 (prod opt-in): selected customer routes on Dedicated pools with manual approval before full apply
rollback_steps: Immediate: VGM issues 'rollback' event for change-id and routes 100% traffic off the change-id in <30s
State: mark change as 'failed' with reason and create postmortem stub in Confluence
Follow-up: revert optimizer suggestion in recommendation store and flag optimizer model for retraining if false positive
Notification: Send alert to #slo-ops and on-call SRE; include metrics snapshot and the offending change-id
monitoring_queries: 95th_latency: query=metrics.p95(latency_ms) by route 1m/5m windows; alert if > route_config.threshold
throughput_drop: compare current 5m requests/sec to 30m baseline; alert if drop > 20%
kl_shift: compute KL divergence over token_length distribution between canary and baseline windows; alert if > 0.2
error_rate: 5xx rate per route; immediate rollback if > 0.5% and rising
